The corrected model uses a differential equation where each reinforcement contributes a fixed fraction of the gap to maximum strength. This yields a simple positive growth function, approximating exponential convergence. The universal lens integrates these into a unified framework where habit strength evolves deterministically yet probabilistically. GSI applies Bayesian updating to refine estimates of habit strength given reinforcement data. GSE models transitions using discrete state updates governed by the kernel. The epistemic trace reveals a dual failure mode: overfitting to early data and underestimating saturation effects. Historical lineage traces back to formalized theories of rote learning, where postulates were iteratively refined. Opposing agents might include noise in reinforcement delivery or individual variation in physiological limits. Anti-collinearity ensures that habit strength does not become redundant with other behavioral metrics.
